familia.translation: [法] 家族, 家长, 户主

familial.definition:
a. relating to or having the characteristics of a family
s. occurring among members of a family usually by heredity
familial.translation:
a. 家族的, 家庭的
[医] 家族的, 全家的

familial autonomic dysfunction.translation: [医] 家族性自主神经机能异常

familial centrolobar sclerosis.translation: [医] 家族性脑中叶硬化, 梅-佩二氏病

familial cholemia.translation: [医] 家族性胆血症, 先天胆血症, 吉耳伯特氏胆血症

familial corneal dystrophy.translation: [医] 家族性角膜营养不良

familial erythroblastic anemia.translation: [医] 家族性成红细胞性贫血, 库利氏贫血

familial hepatitis.translation: [医] 家族性肝炎, 进行性豆状核变性

familial hypoparathyroidism.translation: [医] 家族性甲状旁腺机能减退

familial hypoplastic anemia.translation: [医] 家族性再生不良性贫血

familial microcytic anemia.translation: [医] 家族性小红细胞性贫血

familial multiple telangiectasis.translation: [医] 家族多数性毛细管扩张

familial spherocytosis.translation: [医] 家族性球形红细胞症, 明-肖-根三氏综合征

familial spinal muscular atrophy.translation: [医] 家庭脊髓性肌萎缩, 韦-霍二氏麻痹

familial splenic anemia.translation: [医] 家族性脾性贫血, 高歇氏病

familiar.definition:
n. a person attached to the household of a high official (as a pope or bishop) who renders service in return for support
n. a spirit (usually in animal form) that acts as an assistant to a witch or wizard
a. well known or easily recognized
a. within normal everyday experience; common and ordinary; not strange
familiar.translation:
a. 熟悉的, 常见的, 亲密的
n. 熟友, 常客

familiar with.translation: 熟悉的; 友好的, 过分亲密的

familiarisation.definition: n the experience of becoming familiar with something

familiarise.definition: v make familiar or conversant with

familiarised.definition:
v make familiar or conversant with
s having achieved a comfortable relation with your environment
familiarised.translation:
使众所周知（familiarise的过去式与过去分词形式）
使……熟悉（familiarise的过去式与过去分词形式）

familiarises.definition:
-s form of familiarise
v make familiar or conversant with
familiarises.translation: (familiarise 的第三人称 -s形式) vt.<主英>=familiarize

familiarising.definition:
v make familiar or conversant with
s serving to make familiar

familiarities.translation: n. 熟悉( familiarity的名词复数 ); 通晓; 认识; 友好随便

familiarity.definition:
n. usualness by virtue of being familiar or well known
n. close or warm friendship
n. an act of undue intimacy
familiarity.translation: n. 熟悉, 精通, 亲密

familiarization.definition: n. the experience of becoming familiar with something
familiarization.translation: n. 亲密, 精通, 熟悉

familiarize.definition: v. make familiar or conversant with
familiarize.translation: vt. 使熟悉, 使熟知, 使通俗化

familiarized.translation: v. 使（某人）熟悉, 使通晓( familiarize的过去式和过去分词 )

familiarizes.definition: v make familiar or conversant with
familiarizes.translation: v. 使（某人）熟悉, 使通晓( familiarize的第三人称单数 )

familiarizing.definition: p. pr. & vb. n. of Familiarize
familiarizing.translation: v. 使（某人）熟悉, 使通晓( familiarize的现在分词 )

familiarly.definition: r. in an intimately familiar manner
familiarly.translation: adv. 不拘礼地, 亲密地, 随意地

familiarness.translation: 常见; 熟悉; 日常; 精通

familiars.definition:
n. a person attached to the household of a high official (as a pope or bishop) who renders service in return for support
n. a friend who is frequently in the company of another
n. a spirit (usually in animal form) that acts as an assistant to a witch or wizard
familiars.translation: n. 熟悉的( familiar的复数形式 ); 通晓的; 冒昧的; 随便的

familias.translation: (familia 的复数) [法] 家族, 家长, 户主

familiated.definition:
To be humiliated in front of ones family.
> Its not a good feeling to be familiated.

families.definition:
n a social unit living together
n primary social group; parents and children
n a collection of things sharing a common attribute
n people descended from a common ancestor
n a person having kinship with another or others
n (biology) a taxonomic group containing one or more genera
n a loose affiliation of gangsters in charge of organized criminal activities
n an association of people who share common beliefs or activities

familism.definition: n. The tenets of the Familists.
familism.translation:
n. 家庭主义
[法] 家庭主义

familist.definition:
n. One of afanatical Antinomian sect originating in Holland,
   and existing in England about 1580, called the Family of Love, who held
   that religion consists wholly in love.
